To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the coherence radius is determined by the ratio of the beam width to the turbulence length scale; and the maximum excess is determined by the Fresnel number.
the spatial coherence radius of the laser beam field in the turbulent atmosphere is determined not only by the beam divergence angle, but also by its intensity distribution.

in a turbulent atmosphere, the spatial coherence function for the field of a bounded laser beam is described by a function that has a form different from the function that describes the spatial coherence function in a non-turbulent atmosphere.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of the propagation of a laser beam through a turbulent atmosphere.
a rigorous asymptotic and numeric analysis of the problem of spatial coherence of a laser beam propagated in the turbulent atmosphere.
the problem of the spatial coherence of the field of the radiation of a laser beam that propagates through a turbulent atmosphere.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the coherence radius of a laser beam, as determined by the spatial correlation function, is not an unambiguous quantity.
the coherence radius of a laser beam can be increased by a factor of 2-3 by means of a spatial filter.

the coherence length of the field of laser beams propagating in a strong-turbulence atmosphere is determined by a combination of diffraction and turbulence effects, and the coherence length can be significantly greater than that of plane or spherical waves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spatial coherence function can be used for the analysis of the influence of the atmosphere turbulence on the quality of the image of a distant object.

the coherence radius for a laser beam in the atmosphere is greater than that for a plane wave by a factor of 2.5-3, and for a spherical wave by a factor 2-2.5, while in the case of a spatially unbounded beam the coherence radius is greater by a factor of only 1.5-2.5.
the spatial coherence function has a Gaussian form and its coherence radius is determined by the ratio of the Fresnel zone radius and the rms value of the phase fluctuations of the field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the coherence radius of a laser beam can be increased by a factor of 2 or more compared to the values of this parameter for plane and spherical wave.
the coherence radius of a laser beam increases with the intensity of the fluctuations of the refractive index of the medium and with the beam radius.

the field of a bounded beam in a turbulent medium is more coherent than the field of a plane wave, and that the coherence radius of a bounded beam is larger than the coherence radius for the field of a spherical wave.
